newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 24.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Eight people have offered Auckland man Dean Hunter a kidney free of charge since he said he would pay $10,000 for one. Hunter, 29, said on Wednesday he planned to spend the next few days meeting those people and checking for a close tissue match. Page 1.

NZ First leader Winston Peters has abandoned his vow of silence on coalition talks, agreeing to co-operate with National and Labour on progress reports. On Wednesday, after his first meeting with Labour negotiators and second meeting with National, he said joint statements could be made by the parties as the talks developed. Labour sources said there had been "good atmospherics" at the meeting which lasted an hour and a half. National's negotiating team on Wednesday included Finance Minister Bill Birch and finance and expenditure committee chairman Max Bradford, suggesting that discussions were moving into areas of economic policy. Page 1.

Rugby superstar Jonah Lomu was "gutted" after a Rugby judicial committee found him guilty on Wednesday night of a spear tackle. Lomu was suspended from playing all rugby for one week -- ruling him out of playing in Sunday's national championship first-division rugby final. Page 1.
National MPs Brian Neeson and Bob Simcock on Wednesday clinched their hold on the marginal seats of Waipareira and Hamilton West as the final votes of the election continued to roll in. Page 2.

Australia's failure to win a seat on the United Nations Security Council has left the region without any representation on the UN's most powerful body. Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said on Wednesday the Australian loss was a "bit of a slap in the face" for the region. "We do obviously want recognition for this part of the world." Page 2.
ACT NZ leader Richard Prebble is using the debate over whether New Zealand should buy the next two Anzac frigates to push for an in-depth debate of defence and foreign policy direction. Page 2.

The sale of Forestry Corporation cost the taxpayer $2.8 million in consultants' fees, with the lion's share going to merchant bankers SBC Warburg. The Treasury's annual report, issued on Wednesday, shows the Crown spent $24.1 million on consultants' advice in the past year on a range of issues. Page 12.

The Reserve Bank has sent to all political parties a post-election briefing document which describes the current central bank framework as evolving and "not immutable". However, the 61-page document says the framework is fragile and that any changes to it would be scrutinised carefully both by the public and financial markets. It also says widening the 0-2 percent underlying inflation target would weaken the disciplines on the bank. Page 12.

Bank of New Zealand on Wednesday became the first retail bank to lower lending rates in the wake of interest-rate falls caused by the high New Zealand dollar. BNZ lowered eight of its housing, business and farm lending rates with the three-year fixed rate for home mortgages dropping the most, to 9.25 percent from 9.90 percent. Page 12.

Debt collection company Baycorp Holdings has paid $600,000 for a 30 percent stake in Finance House. Finance House is a new finance company that will lend to clients with credit or security ratings not as strong as those required of traditional lending institutions such as banks. Page 12.

Economists have raised their year-ahead forecasts for the exchange rate, real interest rates and economic growth but lowered their predictions for inflation, a survey by the Alexander Consulting Group shows. Page 12.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD
Surgeons may yet perform an early kidney transplant on Dean Hunter after a flood of calls on Wednesday from would-be donors.
Twelve players from the British rugby league side touring New Zealand have been ordered home early, apparently because of poor crowds and gate takings, and dissatisfaction with the tour's promotion.

Ousted Labour MP Chris Carter does not blame his narrow election defeat in Waipareira on negative reaction to his public declaration of his homosexuality. But he fears the result will send a negative message to other homosexuals in politics. Carter was defeated in the seat by 107 votes.

A series of 26 cut-price charter flights by Sydney-based Seaboard Airlines between Auckland and Sydney, due to start this week, have been delayed as authorities on both sides of the Tasman wait and hear what protection the charter will offer consumers.
Mercury Energy is not about to admit defeat in its takeover bid for Power New Zealand, despite the apparent failure of its most recent push to resolve the stalemate in Power New Zealand's ownership.

Telecom's golden profit run appears set to be broken as problems mount with its loss-making Australian operation, Pacific Star. Earnings are expected to come in below expectation for the first time since listing five years ago when its second-quarter profit is announced on November 14.
The market value of Infratil's power company holdings surged during the six months to September 30, the infrastructure and utilities investor said on Wednesday.
A Fletcher Energy-led joint venture has been named as the preferred developer of a $230 million Island co-generation electricity project in British Columbia.
